ctf.cache.mission: A treasure is hidden in this place… but `ls` can't see it.
ctf.cache.indices: Some objects hide behind the bushes.
Hidden files have a name starting with a dot.
ctf.cache.schema:
📐 Hidden files (behind the bushes)
   `ls`      →  notes.txt
   `ls -a`   →  .  ..  .drapeau  notes.txt
   A name starting with “.” is hidden. Detectives ALWAYS look with `ls -a`.
ctf.meule.mission: The treasure is lost in a log of 3,000 lines.
ctf.meule.indices: Read 3,000 lines by hand? No thanks.
Take the detective's magnifying glass: `grep` looks for a text in a file.
ctf.meule.schema:
📐 `grep`
   journal.log ─┬─ line 1    ✗
                ├─ …         ✗
                └─ line 2047 ✓ TG{…}
   The `grep` magnifying glass reads every line and keeps only the ones that match.
ctf.coffre.mission: The safe has a padlock. But it's YOUR safe…
ctf.coffre.indices: `cat coffre.txt` → access denied. Look at its padlocks (its permissions).
ctf.coffre.schema:
📐 Permissions (the padlocks)
   ----------  →  `chmod 644`  →  -rw-r--r--
   r = read, w = write, x = execute
   The owner always has the key to the padlocks of their files.
ctf.labyrinthe.mission: The treasure is at the far end of a maze of places.
ctf.labyrinthe.indices: Walking to every place by hand would take ages.
`find` looks for an object by name in every place.
ctf.labyrinthe.schema:
📐 `find`
   .  ─ a ─ b ─ c ─ d ─ drapeau.txt ✓
   `find` visits ALL the places (the folder tree) for you.
ctf.code.mission: This message is unreadable… it wears a disguise: base64.
ctf.code.indices: `base64` is a disguise (an encoding), not a real padlock (an encryption).
The `base64` command removes the disguise with -d.
ctf.code.schema:
📐 Disguise ≠ padlock (encoding ≠ encryption)
   “TG{…}” ⇄ `base64` ⇄ “VEd7…==”
   Anyone can decode base64: it protects nothing!
ctf.miroir.indices: Every line is flipped, like in a mirror.
ctf.aiguille.mission: 40 objects. Only one weighs exactly 42 bytes: that's the one.
ctf.aiguille.indices: Compare the weight of the files.
ctf.aiguille.schema:
📐 Size
   `ls -l`  →  -rw------- 1 u0 u0  42 fichier_17.txt
   `find -size` finds files by their weight: handy for the detective's investigation.

ep.rencontre.examiner: Read its card out loud to see its {stats}.
aide.rencontre.examiner: `cat` reads {un_fichier} out loud. The monster's card is placed in {terrain}.
ep.rencontre.repaire: Where does {nom} come from? Look for its lair in every place of {terrain}.
aide.rencontre.repaire: `find` looks for an object in every place, even the tiniest (each {dossier} and its subfolders). It gives you the full path: that's where the monster lives.
ep.fichiers.enclos: Build me a pen: {un_dossier} called “enclos”, right here.
aide.fichiers.enclos: `mkdir` builds a new place (“make directory”: create a folder).
ep.fichiers.gamelle: Put a bowl in my pen: {un_fichier} called “gamelle”.
aide.fichiers.gamelle: `touch` puts down a brand-new object (an empty file). The / separates the place from the object.
ep.fichiers.doudou: Make a photocopy of my doudou.txt (my cuddly toy) in the pen (I want to keep it here too).
aide.fichiers.doudou: `cp` makes a magic photocopy: first the object to copy, then the place to put it. The original doesn't move.
ep.fichiers.renomme: Change the label of vieux_nom.txt: put my name in lowercase, {nom_min}.txt
aide.fichiers.renomme: `mv` carries an object somewhere else; if it stays in the same place, it just changes its label (its name).
epa.fichiers.archive: Pack my whole pen into a suitcase: the archive “enclos.tar.gz”.
aide.fichiers.archive: `tar` packs a whole place into one tightly packed suitcase (an archive): c = create, z = squash (compress), f = name of the suitcase.
ep.reseau.ping: Shout “Ahoy!” at your own world (localhost) and listen for the echo.
aide.reseau.ping: `ping` shouts “Ahoy!” at another world and waits for the echo. localhost = your own world. -c 3 = shout 3 times, then stop.
ep.reseau.hote: What is your world called on the network?
aide.reseau.hote: `hostname` tells the name of your world on the network.
aide.reseau.ip: Every world connected to the network has an address, like a postal address: {ip}. `ip a` shows them all.
ep.processus.ps: Show me who is awake in the world: each {processus}.
aidea.processus.ps: `ps` shows who is awake: every {processus}. `ps -A` shows them all, even the other residents'.
ep.processus.heure: What time is it? Look at the world's clock.
ep.memoire.place: How much room is left in {disque}?
aide.memoire.place: `df` shows the free room in {disque}; -h writes sizes for humans (GB, MB).
aide.memoire.ram: free shows {ram}: a big worktop where programs put their things. -h = readable sizes.
ep.memoire.poids: How heavy is my nest, with everything inside?
aide.memoire.poids: du weighs a place and everything in it; -s = just the total, -h = readable size.
ep.memoire.sac: I hid some things in my bag sac/. How many? Answer me with `echo`.
aide.memoire.sac: `ls sac` looks into the bag. The | is a pipe: it pours the list into `wc -l`, which counts the lines. Then say the number with `echo`.
ep.securite.cage: Make me a cage: {un_fichier} called “cage” in my pen.
aide.securite.cage: `touch` puts down a brand-new object (build the pen first with `mkdir` if it's missing).
ep.securite.cachette: Hide a secret in my pen: {un_fichier} whose name starts with a dot.
aide.securite.cachette: An object whose name starts with a dot is hidden: `ls` doesn't see it, `ls -a` does.
ep.securite.prive: Put a padlock on my cage: nobody but you may touch it.
aide.securite.prive: `chmod` puts on a padlock (it changes the permissions). 600 = only you can read and write, nobody else.
ep.securite.empreinte: Give me the fingerprint of collier.txt (its first 8 characters, with `echo`).
aide.securite.empreinte: `sha256sum` takes the fingerprint of an object: a string of letters and numbers that changes if you change a single letter. Copy the first 8 with `echo`.
aide.code.chant: `echo` says a text. The funnel > writes it on a scroll instead of the screen.
ep.code.script: Write me a little recipe tour.sh that does an echo, then {rendre_executable}.
aide.code.script: A recipe (a script) is a scroll of commands. Write it, then `chmod +x` allows it to cook by itself: it becomes {executable} (you run it with `./tour.sh`).
ep.code.compte: Write the numbers 1 to 5, one per line, in compte.txt (with a loop!).
aide.code.compte: A for loop repeats a command for each number. Everything said lands on the scroll thanks to the funnel >.
ep.materiel.machine: What kind of world is this? Look at {processeur}.
aide.materiel.machine: `uname -m` tells what kind of brain the world has: {processeur} (x86_64, arm64…).
ep.materiel.coeurs: How many cores does {processeur} have? Answer with `echo`.
aide.materiel.coeurs: `nproc` counts the cores of {processeur}: how many things it does at the same time. Then answer with `echo`.
aidea.materiel.disques: `df` shows {disque} and its compartments (the partitions), with the space of each one.
ep.bugs.erreurs: Find the ERROR lines in bug.log.
aide.bugs.erreurs: `grep` is the detective's magnifying glass: it shows the lines that contain the word.
ep.bugs.combien: How many errors are there in bug.log? Answer with `echo`.
aide.bugs.combien: `grep -c` counts the lines found by the magnifying glass, instead of showing them.
ep.bugs.corrige: Make me a corrige.log with all the lines EXCEPT the errors.
aide.bugs.corrige: `grep -v` does the opposite and keeps the lines WITHOUT the word; the funnel > writes them on a new scroll.
ep.nuage.photos: Put three photos in it (photo1.jpg, photo2.jpg, photo3.jpg).
aide.nuage.photos: `touch` can put down several objects at once: write their names one after another.
ep.nuage.copie: Make a photocopy of the whole cloud in “nuage_copie”.
aide.nuage.copie: `cp -r` photocopies a whole place, with everything in it (r = recursive).
ep.donnees.debut: Just read me the top of croquettes.txt.
aide.donnees.debut: `head` reads only the top of the scroll (10 lines).
ep.donnees.lignes: How many lines in croquettes.txt? Answer with `echo`.
aide.donnees.lignes: `wc -l` counts the lines of a scroll. Then answer with `echo`.
ep.donnees.trie: Put croquettes.txt in order, into {un_fichier} trie.txt.
aide.donnees.trie: sort puts the lines in order like a dictionary; the funnel > writes the result on a scroll.
ep.donnees.differentes: How many different kinds of kibble? Answer with `echo`.
aide.donnees.differentes: sort sorts, `uniq` removes twins that follow each other, `wc -l` counts. The pipes | connect them one after another.
ep.crypto.decode: Decode message.b64 and tell me the secret word with `echo`.
aide.crypto.decode: base64 disguises a text as strange letters (it encodes it). `base64 -d` takes the disguise off (d = decode).
ep.ia.bonjour: Say hello to me with my name (with `echo`).
aide.ia.bonjour: `echo` says the text you give it.
ep.ia.chat: How many lines contain “chat” in croquettes.txt? Answer with `echo`.
aide.ia.chat: `grep -c` counts the lines where the magnifying glass finds the word.
ep.ia.frequent: What is the most frequent word in croquettes.txt? Answer with `echo`.
aide.ia.frequent: sort sorts, `uniq -c` counts each word, then `sort -n` sorts by number: the last one is the champion.
ep.retro.record: What is the best score in scores.txt? Answer with `echo`.
aide.retro.record: `sort -n` puts numbers from smallest to biggest; `tail -1` keeps the last one (the biggest).
ep.retro.top3: Write the 3 best scores, from biggest to smallest, in top3.txt.
aide.retro.top3: `sort -nr` sorts from biggest to smallest (r = reversed), `head -3` keeps the first 3, the funnel > writes them on the scroll.
ep.glitch.voir: Look at corrompu.txt… my words are backwards!
ep.glitch.repare: Put corrompu.txt the right way round in repare.txt.
aide.glitch.repare: `rev` flips each line, like in a mirror; the funnel > writes the result on a scroll.
ep.glitch.chuchote: I'm shouting too loud (cri.txt): write it in lowercase in chuchote.txt.
aide.glitch.chuchote: tr changes letters into other letters: here each capital (A-Z) into lowercase (a-z). The < hands it the scroll to read.
ep.systeme.qui: Who are you to the world? Ask for your inhabitant name.
aide.systeme.qui: `whoami` (“who am I?”) tells your resident name: your username.
ep.systeme.systeme: What is the world we live in called (the system)?
aide.systeme.systeme: `uname -a` reads the world's ID card: its name, its version, its kind of brain.
ep.systeme.alias: Give me a command nickname, with my name, using `alias`.
aide.systeme.alias: An alias is a nickname: a short word that runs a longer command. Then type the nickname to try it!
ep.systeme.variable: Put my name in a labelled box called BESTIOLE (an environment variable).
aide.systeme.variable: An environment variable is a little box with a label that the whole terminal can open. export fills it; `echo $BESTIOLE` reads it back.

lec.t0.0.dit: Hi! Let's explore the Terminaworld together. Where is the “you are here” sign?
lec.t0.0.bravo: Found it, there's our “you are here” sign! Grown-ups call it “the folder you're in” (`pwd`).
lec.t0.1.dit: Look around you: what is there in this place?

lec.t1.0.dit: I need a world to play in: the Terminaworld. From your base camp, build a new place!

lec.t1.1.bravo: Here we are! Walking to a place, grown-ups say “change folder”.
lec.t1.2.dit: Build me a little nest here!
lec.t1.2.bravo: It's perfect! A place inside a place: grown-ups say “a subfolder”. And I can hear a noise far away…
lec.t2.0.dit: I'm hungry! Take the funnel “>” and pour an apple onto the scroll repas.txt in my nest.
lec.t2.0.bravo: Yum! Careful: the funnel wipes the scroll before writing. Grown-ups say “write to a file”.
lec.t2.1.dit: Read me the scroll repas.txt out loud.
lec.t2.1.bravo: An apple, perfect! Grown-ups say “display a file”. Always check before you act!
lec.t2.2.dit: Take the detective's magnifying glass: look for the word “pomme” on the scroll.
lec.t2.2.bravo: The magnifying glass found it! Grown-ups say “search in a file”.
lec.t3.0.dit: Who is allowed to touch my meal? Look at the padlocks.
lec.t3.0.bravo: r = read, w = write, x = make it run. Grown-ups say “permissions”.
lec.t3.1.dit: Put a padlock on the scroll so nobody damages it!
lec.t3.1.bravo: Click! You can read it, but not write anymore. Grown-ups say “read-only”.
lec.t3.2.dit: Try adding a pear at the bottom of the scroll, just to see…
lec.t3.2.bravo: Refused! “>>” adds at the bottom without wiping anything… but the padlock holds. Grown-ups say “append”.
lec.t4.0.dit: Make a photocopy of my meal, just in case.
lec.t4.0.bravo: Two identical scrolls, and the original didn't move! Grown-ups say “copy”.
lec.t4.1.dit: Carry the copy to the crossroads and stick a new label on it: reserve.txt.
lec.t4.1.bravo: Carried and renamed in one go! Grown-ups say “move” and “rename”.
lec.t4.2.dit: We don't need it anymore. Careful: this is the shredder, not the bin!
lec.t4.2.bravo: Shredded forever: no bin to get it back. Grown-ups say “delete”. Always check first!

hist.reveil.debut: *knock knock*… Can you hear me? I'm very small and I'm cold. This world, the Terminaworld, has been asleep for so long… Grown-ups call it “the computer”. Come and find me: we'll explore it together!
hist.reveil.fin: *CRACK!* You found me! I'm not alone in the dark anymore. But the world is still asleep, and I can hear monsters snoring far away… First I need a nest of my own.
hist.nid.debut: Brrr, the old hallway is so draughty! Let's build ourselves a nest: {un_dossier} just for us, with a bed and a meal. Commands are our tools, like a hammer and nails.
hist.nid.fin: My nest is perfect and my tummy is full! Listen carefully: seven places of the world are asleep, and in each one a family of monsters has settled. The ancients gave them funny names, written on the signposts. You choose where to start.
hist.grenier.debut: Here's the Attic, a forest where the Sylvans pile up everything they find! Their vines have mixed everything up, and my teddy bear is stuck somewhere. We need the map of the forest, then to tidy, copy and throw away what's no longer needed.
hist.grenier.fin: The forest can breathe! The vines have tidied themselves away and the Sylvans are napping in the branches. You can carry, copy and throw away like a real adventurer.
hist.cave.debut: Shh… can you hear that? Deep in the Cellar, a cavern dug under the mountain, the Demons steal my food at night! To stop them, we need to know who's in charge in this world, then put {droits} on my supplies.
hist.cave.fin: Click, clack, padlock! The Demons tried and broke their teeth. They promised to be good… well, almost.
hist.bibliotheque.debut: At the bottom of the lagoon sleeps a sunken library… and the Book of the Abyss has disappeared! The Abyssals hid it between the seaweed-covered shelves, and without it, we can't read the story of the world. Grab your magnifying glass: let's investigate.
hist.bibliotheque.fin: Book found! The Abyssals even taught us to count lines and search for words. You are a real detective of {fichiers}.
hist.machines.debut: The world is suffocating! At the foot of the volcano, the Elementals have blocked the pipes of the old engine room. Let's look at the room left in {ram} and in {disque}, find what's too heavy… and throw it away.
hist.machines.fin: Vrrrooom! The machines are running again and the Elementals are warming up by the lava. The world is breathing deeply.
hist.dortoir.debut: Woo woo… In the Dormitory, a valley full of mist, ghost {processus} refuse to sleep! The Undead keep waking them up. We'll count them, start one ourselves, then send them to bed.
hist.dortoir.fin: Silence… everyone is asleep under the mist. The Undead yawn and wave at us. You know who is awake in the world, and how to put them to bed.
hist.atelier.debut: In the middle of the scrap-metal hills, in the Workshop, the Constructs build machines that follow recipes all by themselves! We'll write {script}, make it work, give it a nickname… and take photos of our objects with the magic camera, `git`.
hist.atelier.fin: Bzzt! The Constructs clap their pincers. You wrote your own commands and took your first photos of objects. You're a real inventor!
hist.tour.debut: At the very top of the Tower, among clouds and lightning, the Celestials watch {reseau}. Our world is not alone! We'll shout “Ahoy!” to the other worlds, find our address, send the mail carrier and read the directory.
hist.tour.fin: Ahoy, ahoy! The other worlds answered! The Celestials show us the secret tunnel, `ssh`, which we'll open one day. Our world is not alone anymore.
hist.coeur.debut: The heart of the world is beating very softly… The Aberrations scrambled everything: the messages are backwards and the heart is in pieces. You'll need everything you've learned. And deep down, someone enormous is sleeping: Abyssor.
hist.coeur.fin: Boom… boom… BOOM! The heart is beating! Everyone wakes up, the sun rises over every place, and Abyssor opens one eye: “Thank you, little human.” He goes back to sleep with a smile. You woke up the Terminaworld!
hist.telephone.debut: At the edge of the world, there's a garden: your phone! You can turn on its torch, make it vibrate, open apps… Let's go play outside.
hist.telephone.fin: The phone garden has no secrets for you now. You control it from the keyboard, like a pro!
hist.entree.dit: Let's go! Walk to the place {piece}.
hist.reveil1.0.dit: Look around your base camp: an old path is called terrain_terminagotchi. Follow it!
hist.reveil1.0.bravo: Crrrr… So much dust! Here we are at the crossroads of the sleeping Terminaworld.
hist.reveil1.1.dit: It's pitch dark. Look around you: what's here?
hist.reveil1.1.bravo: A signpost: the vestibule, the old entrance of the world. It looks like something warm is waiting for me there…
hist.reveil1.2.bravo: We're in the vestibule, under the old stone arch. Shh…
hist.reveil1.3.bravo: A warm egg! *knock knock*… It's ME! You found me!
hist.nid0.0.dit: I need a nest. Go back one step, to the crossroads: `cd ..` means “I go back one step”.
hist.nid0.2.dit: Put a brand-new object in the nest: it will be my bed.
hist.nid0.2.bravo: A brand-new bed, empty and soft. Grown-ups say “create {un_fichier} that's empty”.
hist.grenier0.1.dit: Vines everywhere! Look at the map of the whole forest at once.
hist.grenier0.1.bravo: So many places inside places! That's {arborescence}.
hist.grenier0.2.dit: My teddy bear is stuck in the mess! Bring it back to the nest.
hist.grenier0.2.bravo: My teddy! `mv` carried it all the way to the nest. “..” means “the place before, going back one step”.
hist.t4.3.dit: Expert challenge: photocopy the whole jumble at once, with all its places.
hist.t4.3.bravo: -r means "with everything inside" (recursive). Well done, expert!
hist.cave0.2.dit: The keeper's key is called `sudo`: it's for big jobs, not for playing. Just read its instructions.
hist.cave0.2.astuce: -h asks for no password. Never give your password to a game!
hist.cave0.2.bravo: `sudo` means "do it as {administrateur}". With it you can fix everything… or break everything. That's why it asks for a password.
hist.biblio0.1.dit: The Book of the Abyss is hidden on a shelf. Ask `find` to look for it everywhere.
hist.biblio0.1.bravo: Found it! `find` searches every place and every place inside places.
hist.biblio0.2.dit: Open the book and read it page by page.
hist.biblio0.2.bravo: What a story! `less` turns the pages one by one.
hist.biblio1.1.dit: Read only the beginning of the book: its first 3 lines.
hist.biblio1.1.bravo: `head` reads the top of the page, like a newspaper headline.
hist.biblio1.2.dit: How many lines does this book have? Count them!
hist.biblio1.2.bravo: `wc` counts lines (-l), words (-w) and letters. Handy for a detective!
hist.biblio1.3.dit: Expert challenge: the word TRESOR is written somewhere in the sunken library. Search all the books at once.
hist.biblio1.3.bravo: -r searches every shelf, -n gives the line number. Bravo, expert!
hist.machines0.1.dit: Listen to the world breathing: how much room is left in {ram}?
hist.machines0.1.bravo: free shows {ram}: the world's worktable. When it's full, everything slows down!
hist.machines0.2.dit: Something heavy is blocking the pipes. Weigh everything in this place.
hist.machines0.2.bravo: vieux_carton.bin is heavy! That's the culprit.
hist.machines0.3.dit: Throw away that old box (only that one, and only here!).
hist.machines0.3.bravo: Phew! The world breathes better. There's room again in {disque}.
hist.atelier0.1.dit: The Constructs left a plan on the workbench. Read it!
hist.atelier0.1.bravo: A three-step plan: write a recipe, make it work, and take a photo of everything. Let's get to work!
hist.tour2.1.dit: To get into another world, there's a secret tunnel: `ssh`. We won't open it today, just ask it who it is.
hist.tour2.1.bravo: `ssh` links two worlds with an encrypted tunnel. You need the other world's key to get in.
hist.coeur0.1.dit: This message is written backwards! Turn it around with `rev`.
hist.coeur0.1.bravo: `rev` put everything the right way round: the message talks about a secret passage, right here!
hist.coeur0.2.dit: A secret passage? It's hidden: look for the secret passages.
hist.coeur0.2.bravo: There it is: .porte_secrete! A name starting with a dot is {cache}.
hist.coeur0.3.bravo: Brrr, it's dark… There's a piece of the heart, and someone huge sleeping.
hist.coeur1.0.dit: The heart is in three pieces, scattered across the world! Look for all the fragment objects.
hist.coeur1.0.bravo: Three pieces: one here, one in the Attic Forest, one in the Tower.
hist.coeur1.1.dit: Glue the three pieces into one file: `cat` reads them one after the other, > pours them into coeur_repare.txt.
hist.coeur1.1.bravo: The three pieces are together again! The heart goes "boom", very softly.
hist.coeur1.2.dit: Protect the mended heart, so the Aberrations can never scramble it again.
hist.coeur1.2.bravo: Click! The heart is under lock.
hist.coeur2.0.dit: Abyssor, the mythical guardian, talks in his sleep. Listen to what he says.
hist.coeur2.0.bravo: He wants to know how many scratches he left in the world.
hist.coeur2.1.dit: Count the files where his name is written in CAPITALS: `grep` finds, `wc -l` counts, and the pipe | passes from one to the other.
hist.coeur2.1.bravo: The pipe | plugs two commands together. Remember that number!
hist.coeur2.2.dit: Write your answer (the number, instead of the ?) in coeur/reponse.txt.
hist.coeur2.2.bravo: "That is right", rumbles Abyssor. His eyes shine like stars.
hist.lecon.finie.dit: Lesson finished! We're doing great, you and me.

hist.coeur.ouvert.dit: Five places awake! I can hear something beating in the middle of the world… The heart has opened: `cd ~/terrain_terminagotchi/coeur`
hist.fin.dit: The whole Terminaworld is awake, thanks to you! But a world is big: there are still lots of letters, secret passages and quests to find. Shall we go on?

hist.meuble.abysses: Once upon a time there was a world that fell asleep: the Terminaworld.
Demons slept in its Cellar, Sylvans in the Attic Forest.
Deep down, under the heart of the world, slept Abyssor, the guardian.
He would only wake up on the day the whole world beat again.
A child and their creature would come, people said, to wake it.
They would have commands for tools, and courage for light.
The TRESOR of this world is not gold: it's the friends you find there.

qu.q01.texte:
✉ Welcome letter
Welcome, little explorer! This world hides secret passages. Their names start with a dot, so you can't see them… except with `ls -a`!
There's one right here, in the vestibule. Find it and go inside (`cd`).
qu.q02.texte: 🗝 Well done, you found the secret cupboard of the old vestibule! The former inhabitants kept their umbrellas here. There are other secret passages in the world…
qu.q03.texte:
✉ Note from the mail carrier
Hello! I don't know where to drop off the mail. Can you build a mailbox in the vestibule? A place called boite_aux_lettres will do (`mkdir`).
qu.q04.texte: 🐾 Hi, it's Pantoufle, a little Monstrous Beast! My paws are cold on these old stones. Will you put down a rug for me? An object tapis.txt in the vestibule would be perfect (`touch`).
qu.q05.texte: 🕰 The vestibule clock has stopped. Ask the world for the time and write it in vestibule/heure.txt: `date > vestibule/heure.txt`
qu.q06.texte:
🛒 Shopping list
Write at least three things to eat in nid/courses.txt, one per line. Tip: `echo apple >> nid/courses.txt` adds a line at the end.
qu.q07.texte: 🐾 I'm Grignote, the vestibule mouse. Your nest looks so cosy… Will you make me a cushion? An object nid/coussin.txt will do.
qu.q08.texte: 🧸 Under the bed there are always forgotten treasures… and dust bunnies. You found a hideout!
qu.q09.texte:
📜 Grandma's recipe
Sunday cake: 2 apples, 1 smile, a pinch of patience.
Make a copy of it in your nest, just in case: `cp nid/recette_de_mamie.txt nid/recette_copie.txt`
qu.q10.texte: 📔 A diary page is waiting for you: nid/journal_intime.txt. Add a sentence about your day at the end, with >> (with a single >, you wipe everything!).
qu.q10.page:
Dear diary,
Today I found an egg.
qu.q11.texte: 🐾 Hello, I'm Mousseline the Sylvan! The vines hid my 3 socks in the Attic Forest. Bring them all back to grenier/panier/. Tip: `find grenier -name "chaussette*"` (even the hidden corners!).
qu.q12.texte: 🦉 Hoo hoo! You found the owl's secret nest, high up in the branches. It leaves you a feather as a keepsake.
qu.q13.texte:
✉ Letter from the gardener
The vines grew leaves in grenier/lianes/. How many are there? Count them (`ls`, or `ls | wc -l`) and write the number in grenier/reponse_jardinier.txt.
qu.q14.texte: 🐾 It's Ronce! My photos are lying around in the mess. Put all the photo_*.txt into grenier/album/. Tip: `mv` moves several files at once with *.
qu.q15.texte:
📢 THEFT NOTICE
A cake has disappeared! It was seen heading for a barrel in the Cellar… Find gateau.txt (`find`) and bring it back to the nest.
qu.q16.texte: 🐾 I'm Braise, a little Demon… a nice one! I'd like a chest that nobody can damage. Create cave/coffre.txt, then put a padlock on it (`chmod 444`).
qu.q17.texte: 🕳 A trapdoor under the cavern's barrels! It's cold down there and smells of cheese. A crystal shines in a corner.
qu.q18.texte:
📋 Inventory to check
How many lines are there in cave/inventaire.txt? Count them with `wc -l` and write the number in cave/reponse_inventaire.txt.
qu.q18.choses: apples, pears, carrots, cheese, jam, honey, bread, nuts, milk, eggs, soup, biscuits
qu.q19.texte:
🌲 Map of the foundations
Under the Terminaworld lie the foundations of the whole computer: the folder /. Look at them with `ls /`… but touch nothing: these are the wild lands!
qu.q20.texte: 🐾 Bloop! It's Glouglou the Abyssal. I forgot the magic word of my aquarium! It's written in a diary on shelf b, after “MOT MAGIQUE”. Find it (`grep`) and write it in bibliotheque/mot_magique.txt.
qu.q20.journal:
Glouglou's logbook
Monday: I swam.
Tuesday: I swam again.
qu.q21.texte:
📚 Library card
The titles in bibliotheque/titres.txt are in a muddle. Put them in alphabetical order in bibliotheque/titres_ranges.txt: `sort bibliotheque/titres.txt > bibliotheque/titres_ranges.txt`
qu.q21.titres: The greedy dragon, A mouse on the moon, Zebedee the zebra, The pirates of the lagoon, My friend the robot, Goodnight ghosts, Alice and the golden key, Journey to the bottom of the volcano
qu.q22.texte: 📜 The archive cave, under the sunken library! Scrolls so old they crackle when you touch them. The Abyssals hide their secrets here.
qu.q23.texte: 📖 The big book is far too long to read all of it! Read only the beginning of bibliotheque/grand_livre.txt with `head`.
qu.q23.page: Page {n}: and the story goes on…
qu.q24.texte: 🐾 Bzzt! It's Étincelle the Elemental. Is the world's big chest full? Check the free space with `df -h`, here, in the engine room.
qu.q25.texte:
🔧 Note from the heating engineer
One of the pipes (rouge, bleu or vert) in salle_des_machines/tuyaux/ is blocked by something heavy. Weigh them with `du -sh`, then write the name of the heaviest folder in salle_des_machines/reponse_tuyau.txt.
qu.q26.texte: 🔥 The secret boiler room, right next to the lava! This is where the chilliest Elementals sleep. It's so cosy you could stay for hours.
qu.q27.texte: 🐾 I'm Givre, and I'm melting! Build me a fridge in the engine room (salle_des_machines/frigo) and put a glacon.txt in it.
qu.q28.texte: 🌲 On the boiler, a plate says: “My real name is written in /etc/os-release”. Read it with `cat` (look, don't touch: these are the wild lands).
qu.q29.texte: 🐾 Oooh… I'm a friendly Undead. I can't count the awake programs, there are too many! Count them for me: `ps aux | wc -l`
qu.q30.texte:
🕯 Night watch diary
The night watchman wants to know the name of this world's boss. Ask `whoami` and write the answer in dortoir/veilleur.txt: `whoami > dortoir/veilleur.txt`
qu.q31.texte: 👻 Boo! Under the mist, there was… only a forgotten shooting star. The Undead use it as a night light.
qu.q32.texte: 🌙 Ghosts only fall asleep with a story. Read them dortoir/conte_du_soir.txt page by page, with `less` (q to close).
qu.q32.conte: Page {n}. The little ghost yawned, then yawned again…
qu.q33.texte: ⏰ The alarm clock wonders how long the world has been awake. Ask with `uptime`.
qu.q34.texte: 🐾 Beep! I'm Boulon the Construct. Write a recipe atelier/bonjour.`sh` that says hello (`echo 'echo Hello!' > atelier/bonjour.sh`), then run it with sh.
qu.q35.texte:
📐 Secret plan
The machine atelier/machine.sh won't start: it isn't allowed to! Make it executable (`chmod +x`), then try it: `./atelier/machine.sh`
qu.q36.texte: 🔩 Under the workbench, a hideout full of golden bolts! The Constructs keep their most precious bits here.
qu.q37.texte:
📷 Logbook
An album with only one photo is sad! Change a file in the carnet, then take a second photo: `git add`, then `git commit -m "second memory"`.
qu.q38.texte: 🐾 It's Nuage the Celestial! Did you know our world has an address all of its own, 127.0.0.1? Shout “Ahoy!” at it: `ping -c 1 127.0.0.1`
qu.q39.titre: The map of the wild lands
qu.q39.texte:
🌲 Map of the wild lands
Beyond the Terminaworld lies the whole computer. Its name is written in /etc/hostname: read it with `cat`. Out there, we look but touch nothing!
qu.q40.texte: 🔭 A secret observatory, at the very top of the Tower, above the clouds! A telescope points at the other worlds of the internet.
qu.q41.texte:
📨 Telegram
What is the address of the world example.com? Ask the directory (`nslookup example.com`) and write the address in tour/adresse.txt.
qu.q42.texte: 🐾 Olleh! … Sorry: hello! I'm Bizarre the Aberration, I speak backwards. Write "terminagotchi" backwards in coeur/envers.txt: `echo terminagotchi | rev > coeur/envers.txt`
qu.q43.texte: 🔊 The echo chamber, a cave deep in the heart of the world… echo… echo… Here, everything you say comes back three times… times… times…
qu.q44.texte:
✉ Last message
How many words are in the scrambled message coeur/message_brouille.txt? Count them with `wc -w` and write the number in coeur/reponse_mots.txt.
